items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: David Mott — I mean all kinds of people. So there were a lot of © Fillius Jazz Archive -5- musicians around, a lot of opportunities to play with like-minded players

ctx.x: Oh gee, Anthony Davis, George Lewis, Gerry Hemingway, Mark Dresser, Leo Smith, Bobby Naughton, Mario Pavone. It was an interesting time. These are all very highly regarded jazz artists, and interesting innovative thinkers too, and they all happened to be there at that one time. David Mott — I mean all kinds of people. So there were a lot of © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

musicians around, a lot of opportunities to play with like-minded players, and we created a scene there, at the clubs and the concert scene. So there was a little burst of activity in New Haven during the 70s. And it was I guess my training ground.
